title: Timed conditional composition
statement: Let $D$, $M_1$, and $M_2$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, let $p$ be a predicate on Boolean words, let $f_1,f_2$ map Boolean words to Boolean words, and let $T_0,T_1,T_2 : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. If $D$ computes the one-bit word $[p(x)]$ on every input $x$ in time $T_0(|x|)$, and $M_i$ computes $f_i(x)$ in time $T_i(|x|)$ for each $i\in\{1,2\}$, then there are a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $M$ computes $f_1(x)$ when $p(x)$ is true and $f_2(x)$ otherwise, in time $c\bigl(T_0(|x|)+\max(T_1(|x|),T_2(|x|))+1\bigr)$ on every input $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $D$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
$M_1$ and $M_2$ are finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet
$f_1,f_2$ map Boolean words to Boolean words
$T_0,T_1,T_2$ map natural numbers to natural numbers

Let $D$, $M_1$, $M_2$ be finite-state Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, let $p$
be a Boolean predicate on Boolean words, $f_1$ and $f_2$ functions from Boolean words to
Boolean words, and $T_0, T_1, T_2 : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. Suppose that on every input
$x$, $D$ halts within $T_0(|x|)$ steps with output the one-bit word $p(x)$, $M_1$ halts
within $T_1(|x|)$ steps with output $f_1(x)$, and $M_2$ halts within $T_2(|x|)$ steps with
output $f_2(x)$. Then there exist a finite-state Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean
alphabet and a constant $c \in \mathbb{N}$ such that on every input $x$, $M$ halts within
$c \cdot (T_0(|x|) + \max(T_1(|x|), T_2(|x|)) + 1)$ steps with output $f_1(x)$ if $p(x)$
holds and $f_2(x)$ otherwise.
